title: Decimals (Tenths and Hundredths)
description: Master decimals for Class 4 Maths. Convert fractions to decimals, compare tenths and hundredths, add and subtract decimals. Real-life examples with rupees and measurement. 10 MCQs and 6 IMO questions.

topics.title: Fractions as Decimals
topics.concept:
A decimal is another way to write a fraction. A decimal point separates the whole number part from the fractional part.

  • Tenths place: first digit after decimal = denominator 10 (e.g. 3/10 = 0.3)
  • Hundredths place: second digit after decimal = denominator 100 (e.g. 25/100 = 0.25)

Think of it like Indian currency: Rs.1 = 100 paise. 10 paise = 10/100 = 0.10. 1 paisa = 1/100 = 0.01.

Converting fractions to decimals: Make the denominator 10 or 100, then write in decimal form. Adding a zero to the right of a decimal does NOT change its value: 0.3 = 0.30.

examples.solution: Denominator is 10, so we need 1 digit after decimal point. Numerator is 7. Write as 0.7. Check: 0.7 means 7 tenths = 7/10.

examples.problem: Write 0.45 as a fraction in simplest form.
examples.solution: 0.45 has 2 decimal places (hundredths). Write as 45/100. Simplify by dividing by 5: 9/20. Check: 9 and 20 have no common factor except 1. Answer: 9/20.

Hundredths: second place after decimal point, denominator 100

Adding zeros to the right of a decimal does NOT change its value: 0.3 = 0.30

topics.title: Compare Decimals
topics.concept:
Comparing decimals: line up the decimal points and compare digit by digit from left to right.

Steps:

  • Line up the decimal points (add zeros if needed)
  • Compare the ones place first
  • If same, compare tenths
  • If same, compare hundredths
  • The first place where digits differ decides which is larger

Important: 0.3 = 0.30 (adding a zero on the right does not change the value, it just allows comparison).
topics.visual: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 160' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='max-width:100%;font-family:sans-serif'><rect width='480' height='160' fill='#f0fdf4' rx='8'/><text stroke="none" x='240' y='20' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' fill='#065f46' text-anchor='middle'>Comparing 0.45 and 0.4</text><rect x='30' y='35' width='180' height='90' fill='#bbf7d0' rx='6'/><text stroke="none" x='120' y='55' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#065f46' text-anchor='middle'>0.45</text><text stroke="none" x='120' y='75' font-size='11' fill='#047857' text-anchor='middle'>Tenths: 4</text><text stroke="none" x='120' y='95' font-size='11' fill='#047857' text-anchor='middle'>Hundredths: 5</text><rect x='270' y='35' width='180' height='90' fill='#d1fae5' rx='6'/><text stroke="none" x='360' y='55' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' fill='#065f46' text-anchor='middle'>0.40</text><text stroke="none" x='360' y='75' font-size='11' fill='#047857' text-anchor='middle'>Tenths: 4 (SAME)</text><text stroke="none" x='360' y='95' font-size='11' fill='#dc2626' text-anchor='middle'>Hundredths: 0</text><text stroke="none" x='240' y='148' font-size='14' font-weight='bold' fill='#065f46' text-anchor='middle'>Hundredths 5 > 0, so 0.45 > 0.4</text></svg>

examples.solution: Write 0.6 as 0.60. Compare tenths: 6 vs 5. 6 > 5, so 0.6 > 0.59.
Compare ones: 1 vs 0. Since 1 > 0, answer is 1.25 > 0.98. (No need to compare further.)

examples.problem: Riya ran 100m in 14.5 seconds. Priya ran in 14.45 seconds. Who was faster?
examples.solution: In racing, smaller time = faster. Compare 14.5 and 14.45: write 14.50. Tenths: 5 vs 4. 5 > 4, so 14.5 > 14.45. Priya's time (14.45) is less, so Priya was faster.

recap: Always line up decimal points before comparing
Compare left to right: ones, tenths, hundredths
Add zeros to the right when needed for comparison — value stays the same
In real-life problems, read carefully — smaller time = faster!

topics.title: Add and Subtract Decimals
topics.concept:
The most important rule for adding/subtracting decimals: ALWAYS line up the decimal points!

Column Method Steps:

  • Write numbers with decimal points aligned
  • Add zeros to make same number of decimal places
  • Add or subtract from RIGHT to LEFT (like whole numbers)
  • Bring the decimal point STRAIGHT DOWN into the answer
  • Carry or borrow just like with whole numbers
topics.visual: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 160' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='max-width:100%;font-family:sans-serif'><rect width='480' height='160' fill='#eff6ff' rx='8'/><text stroke="none" x='240' y='20' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' fill='#1e3a8a' text-anchor='middle'>Adding Decimals: 4.25 + 0.75 = 5.00</text><text stroke="none" x='160' y='50' font-size='16' fill='#374151' text-anchor='end'>4.25</text><text stroke="none" x='160' y='75' font-size='16' fill='#374151' text-anchor='end'>+  0.75</text><line x1='30' y1='85' x2='200' y2='85' stroke='#374151' stroke-width='1.5'/><text stroke="none" x='160' y='105' font-size='18' font-weight='bold' fill='#1d4ed8' text-anchor='end'>5.00</text><text stroke="none" x='280' y='55' font-size='11' fill='#dc2626'>Hundredths: 5+5=10, write 0 carry 1</text><text stroke="none" x='280' y='75' font-size='11' fill='#059669'>Tenths: 2+7+1=10, write 0 carry 1</text><text stroke="none" x='280' y='95' font-size='11' fill='#1d4ed8'>Ones: 4+0+1=5</text><text stroke="none" x='280' y='115' font-size='11' fill='#b45309'>Decimal point goes straight down</text><text stroke="none" x='240' y='148' font-size='14' font-weight='bold' fill='#065f46' text-anchor='middle'>4.25 + 0.75 = 5.00</text></svg>

examples.solution: Line up decimals: 4.25 + 0.75. Hundredths: 5+5=10 (write 0, carry 1). Tenths: 2+7+1=10 (write 0, carry 1). Ones: 4+0+1=5. Answer: 5.00 = 5.
Write 3.8 as 3.80. Hundredths: 0-5 (borrow): 10-5=5. Tenths: 7-3=4. Ones: 3-1=2. Answer: 2.45.

examples.problem: Riya bought a notebook for Rs.25.50 and a pen for Rs.12.75. She paid Rs.50. How much change?

recap: ALWAYS line up decimal points — this is the most important rule
Add zeros to make all decimals have the same number of places
Carry and borrow exactly as you would with whole numbers
Bring the decimal point straight down into the answer

The sum of two decimals is 3.5. Their difference is 0.7. The smaller decimal is:
questions.explanation: Let x and y where x>y. x+y=3.5 and x-y=0.7. Adding: 2x=4.2, x=2.1. y=3.5-2.1=1.4. Smaller is 1.4.
